messages:
alex: starting smoke onboarding for quasar13b (13B) int4. quant: per-tensor scale+zero, group=128. tests: summarization, long-context regen, open-domain chat.
priya: nice. any known exporter quirks for quasar? is it Llama-style head layout or split like mistral/gemma?
sven: quasar checkpoint uses contiguous-head (all head dims packed) but the converter we used had an option for head-interleave; double-checking.
alex: initial run: stable for short prompts but for >3k tokens we see attention drifting and token duplication. example output: "We observed a significant rise... We observed a significant rise...". also p95 latency is fine (160ms A100) so likely correctness not perf.
ingest-bot: ingest-log: convert_job=888 status=complete flags=[reorder=head-interleave, quant=gptq-lite]
priya: that reorder flag stands out — if checkpoint was contiguous-head we introduced a swap. can you run a compare against fp16 reference with same seed + deterministic sampling?
alex: running: `compare-outputs --ref fp16/quasar13b.ckpt --cand quant/quasar13b-int4.ckpt --prompts smoke_prompts.txt --seed 7 --no-sample --max-tokens 200`
ci-bot: compare-outputs job/7765432100-1: finished. diffs: 18/50 prompts exact match, 32 partial. notable: KV divergence at step ~3136 in many prompts.
sven: KV divergence around 3k tokens again. earlier project had head-order swap causing rotary phase sign flips after a certain token index due to head packing mismatch. check rotary tables and head offset maps.
alex: dumping rotary tables shows phase coefficients identical but when I compute headwise dot they flip sign for heads 8..15. quick python to check:
```python
# pseudo
for h in range(nheads):
    phase_h = sum(rotary_cos[h*hdim:(h+1)*hdim] * ref_cos[h*hdim:(h+1)*hdim])
    if phase_h < 0:
        print('flip', h)
```
# output: flip 8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15
```

priya: that pattern suggests a half-block endian or head-order inversion on second half of heads. maybe converter interpreted head stride as bytes per-head vs floats per-head. Does your quant step cast via uint8 pack that could reorder?
alex: quant script uses packed-int4 with byte-swap=auto. i'll force no-swap and re-convert.
alex: re-run with `convert --no-byte-swap --preserve-head-order --fix-rotary-phase`
ci-bot: convert job/7765432100-2: success.
alex: re-ran compare-outputs. now 46/50 exact matches, KV divergence gone up to 12k tokens. rouge on cnn recovered +2. small remaining quality gap ~0.7 rouge.
sven: progress. likely remaining gap due to attention-proj axis packing during quant scale calibration. also double-check tokenizer special tokens — quasar had an extra <hl> sentinel mapped to id 3; some exporters remapped it to a different slot causing off-by-one when using legacy tokenizer shards. that would manifest as occasional odd repeat when sentinel inserted.
priya: please add ingestion-time check: assert tokenizer.specials['<hl>'] == expected_id and fail ingestion with clear error.
alex: will add check + unit test. opening PR with conversion flags defaulted to --no-byte-swap for known quasar family. tagging follow-up: ONBD-1292 check-proj-axis-quant and ONBD-1293 tokenizer-sentinel-sanity.
ingest-bot: ticket created ONBD-1292 ONBD-1293.
priya: thanks all. next steps: add headwise-rotary-continuity test to CI (compare cosine/sine across head boundaries), add quant pack sanity for byte-order, and update onboarding checklist.
alex: updated smoke-run notes and attaching diff logs to ticket. marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
summary: Quasar13b int4 onboarding revealed headpack/byte-order induced rotary sign flips and tokenizer sentinel id remap; fixed with no-byte-swap + preserve-head-order; follow-ups to validate proj axis packing and tokenizer sanity added.
